Subject: Persistent checkout tail-latency in us-west-2 — we hit repeated timeouts

Hi Nikhil / Grace,

We saw a pronounced increase in checkout failures between ~15:32–16:10 PST today (us-west-2). 95th/99th latencies jumped to 1.8s / 6.2s respectively and some customers reported client timeouts. This impacted a subset of cart checkout flows (CreditCard auth, third-party payment step).

Can you confirm whether this is considered an SLO breach and what remedy/credits are available? We need an ETA on a postmortem and any logs you can share for our audit.

Attached a short CSV showing transaction counts per minute and sample request ids.

Thanks,
Jesse
Head of Platform Ops
FastRetail Co

Subject: Fwd: Persistent checkout tail-latency in us-west-2 — please triage (FR-4827)

David — please see fastRetail ticket FR-4827 (Jesse). They reported sustained p95/p99 latency spikes in us-west-2 during 15:32–16:10 PST. Attached: customer CSV and our trace instructions.

What we saw in the public dashboards (preliminary): a tail-latency climb coincident with increased queue times on the GPU inference pool for model-rewrite v2.3. There are also elevated KV cache eviction counts for the same hosts.

Impact: checkout timeouts, some rate-limited retries, drop in success rate ~0.8–1.2% for that window. Customer is asking about SLA credit eligibility and wants an RCA.

Can you confirm whether this is likely a serving regression or transient infra noise? If it looks like an SLO-qualifying outage, we'll need an estimated downtime window and a draft postmortem for Jesse within 72 hours.

I've started a support export and pinned the raw traces to /exports/FR-4827/raw-traces; attaching the tar we pulled.

Thanks,
Nikhil
[Attachment: raw-traces-usw2-20290111.tar.gz (application/gzip)]
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jan 2029 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent checkout tail-latency in us-west-2 — please triage (FR-4827)

Quick summary from initial triage:
- We reproduced elevated p95/p99 using the customer's request IDs correlated to our traces.
- Root cause (preliminary): a memory leak in a GPU worker process handling model-rewrite v2.3. The leak causes periodic OOMs and process restarts; during restart those hosts have cache cold-starts which push tail latencies up, especially for long-tail checkout flows that depend on cached KV entries.
- Affected hosts: gpu-pool-usw2-a[03-07] (5 hosts).
- Probable impact window (based on restart timestamps and error logs): 2029-01-11T15:34:12-08:00 to 2029-01-11T16:06:47-08:00.

Action taken: we applied an emergency restart policy to the pool and rolled back v2.3 -> v2.2 to stop recurrence. We also increased warmup concurrency to reduce cold-cache penalties.

Next steps: full RCA (with heap profiles, stack traces, and a timeline) — target draft by 2029-01-14 18:00 PST. Because this is an availability impact that caused elevated 5xxs/timeouts and customer-visible retries, this meets our SLO breach criteria for proportional credit.

Attaching initial triage notes.

-David
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial-rca-notes.md (text/markdown)]
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Jesse Park <jesse.park@fastretailco.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2029 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Persistent checkout tail-latency in us-west-2 — credit eligibility and RCA request

Hi Jesse — following up with the confirmed findings and next steps.

Summary:
- Confirmed impact window: 2029-01-11T15:34:12-08:00 to 2029-01-11T16:06:47-08:00 (us-west-2).
- Cause (prelim): memory leak in GPU worker for model-rewrite v2.3 -> periodic OOM/restarts -> cache cold-starts -> elevated p95/p99 tail latency and client timeouts.
- Customer-visible impact: checkout success rate drop ~0.8–1.2% for affected shard(s).

Credit eligibility & remedy:
- Per our SLA, this qualifies as a service availability incident affecting request success/light SLOs. We're proposing a 10% pro-rata credit for the monthly usage attributed to affected requests during the window. Finance will apply the credit to your next invoice; if you prefer a one-time payment or account balance, we can accommodate.

Postmortem & evidence:
- Draft postmortem attached for your review (redwood-postmortem-draft-20290115.docx). It includes timeline, root cause analysis, remediation, and compensating controls.
- Raw traces and a sanitized log bundle are attached to this thread for your audit.

Requested confirmation from you:
1) Please confirm the window above is the correct one to use for the claim.
2) Please confirm acceptance of the proposed 10% pro-rata credit or state an alternative remediation you'd prefer.
3) If you want deeper artifacts (heap dumps, full core files), we can share under an NDA — let me know and we will route that to legal.

We're sorry for the incident. We're treating this as a high priority: David's team will follow up with a final RCA and permanent fix timeline; product and runtime teams are putting a guardrail to prevent similar leaks in the immediate future.

If you approve the credit and the postmortem, we'll finalize the paperwork and schedule a 30-minute readout if you'd like.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[note: attachments include sanitized raw traces and the postmortem draft]
